extracted.intended_audience: general public; journalists and researchers interested in media ethics and Georgian politics
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive Wikipedia article documenting a specific televised fake-news / simulated report (the 13 March 2010 Imedi TV hoax), its content, effects, reactions, and related legal/ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present simulations as genuine breaking news
rubrics_metrics.description: The fake news broadcast was presented as a Chronicle breaking news report and heavily used footage from the Russo-Georgian War; its close resemblance to genuine news programming caused widespread panic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid packaging simulated content in the exact visual/aural style, branding, and timeslot of a real news programme. Presentations that mimic a station's main news bulletin are likely to be interpreted as live events and can cause public harm (example: Imedi aired the simulation in Chronicle's timeslot and used Chronicle presentation elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible on-screen notification that content is a simulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Airing the report as if it were genuine news would be a violation of the Georgian Law on Broadcasting, and [a broadcaster] stated that a notification should be carried on screen telling viewers of the fake report that it was a simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry persistent, visible captions or notifications during any dramatization/simulation to ensure viewers understand the content is not real. A single brief disclaimer at start or end is insufficient if viewers miss it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and clarity of disclaimers (beginning/end may be insufficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the beginning and end of the program noted the events of the broadcast were a fictional 'simulation', the rest of the broadcast did not; many Georgians did not see the disclaimer at the beginning and assumed the events were real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers should be prominent throughout the programme; intermittent or only-start/end notices can be missed and fail to prevent misunderstanding. Best practice: persistent on-screen label and repeated audio reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reuse archival/war footage to portray fabricated current events
rubrics_metrics.description: The fake broadcast 'heavily used footage from the Russo-Georgian War' and used archive footage of foreign diplomats to imply involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repurposing archival footage (especially combat footage) without clear labeling; using such footage to depict fabricated contemporary events misleads viewers and risks inflaming tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scheduling simulations in a regular news timeslot
rubrics_metrics.description: Imedi moved its timeslot forward to 7:59 pm, the timeslot allocated to Chronicle (its regular news programme), causing confusion because Chronicle is a major source of information for viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not air dramatizations in the exact timeslot of a station's principal news bulletin. Scheduling choices that overlap established news slots increase the chance audiences will interpret fiction as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with broadcaster codes of conduct and broadcasting law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Georgian National Communications Commission and the Young Lawyers' Association of Georgia said Imedi had violated the code with its broadcast; airing the report as genuine would violate the Georgian Law on Broadcasting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasters must follow national broadcasting laws and industry codes of conduct; failure can trigger regulatory findings and directives (example: GNMC directed the broadcaster to make a public apology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic ethics: avoid creating public panic and harm
rubrics_metrics.description: The broadcast's close resemblance to genuine news programming caused widespread panic — thousands of emergency calls, ATM runs, mobile network crashes, army units taking defensive positions — and was linked to at least three deaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic ethics require minimizing foreseeable public harm. Content creators should assess risks of panic, physical danger, or destabilisation before airing material that could be mistaken for reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and disciplinary consequences: apologies, sanctions, and lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: After a finding by the GNMC that the broadcast violated the broadcaster's code of conduct, the broadcaster was directed to make a public apology; Russian media announced intent to sue for copyright infringement; opposition parties announced lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect regulatory directives (public apologies), potential civil suits (e.g., copyright, defamation), and internal or industry sanctions where ethical or legal norms are breached. New laws may limit penalties, but reputational and legal risks remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permission / respect copyright and consent for archive footage and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Russian media outlets announced intent to sue Imedi for copyright infringement after the Georgian station used footage without permission from the Russian copyright holders; ambassadors complained about use of their images without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure rights to archival footage and obtain consent or ensure legitimate fair use before using images of identifiable persons (especially diplomats). Misuse can prompt copyright suits and diplomatic complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about production and possible political involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The hoax drew criticism and accusations that then-President Saakashvili and government officials had been informed or involved; taped telephone recordings allegedly implicated officials, intensifying calls for investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media organisations should be transparent about the genesis and funding of high-impact programmes; concealment or perceived government involvement damages credibility and can prompt political and legal fallout. Where allegations arise, independent investigations (including parliamentary commissions or regulatory inquiries) may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate leaked audio recordings with expert analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent analyst recommended expert analysis to determine authenticity of alleged telephone recordings; Irakli Sesiashvili said the recording was 'very close' to authentic but advised forensic checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When audio tapes surface that could assign responsibility or inflame controversy, commission forensic/authenticity analysis (including participation of independent/foreign experts) before relying on or publishing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider regional security and diplomatic repercussions before airing provocative content
rubrics_metrics.description: EU monitors, NATO and various foreign ambassadors called the airing irresponsible and warned it could destabilise the region and harm Georgia's international reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should evaluate whether content could escalate international tensions, endanger peace processes, or harm diplomatic relations; potential geopolitical consequences should inform editorial decisions on airing sensitive simulations.
